arguments.summary: The Fed should hike 25bp: markets widely expect it, CPI all but locks it in, the bar for disappointing is high, and holding would be unprecedented.
The Fed must choose between hiking and risking a large bond spike, because not hiking risks a disorderly long end move and the bond likes orthodoxy.
Without a hike, the 30Y could quickly test 5.75%, a hold would twist steepen the curve, and buybacks would be futile, so a disorderly long end move is likely.
Treasury buybacks would likely fail to stop the long end move: they stumbled out of the gate, and orthodoxy does not rely on buybacks.
A surprise hold would sharply twist steepen the curve through a lower policy path, a high bar to hike, inflation risk premium and a Warsh credibility discount.
Friday's twist flattening shows the bond likes orthodoxy, meaning rate hikes to slow inflation and quell long end spikes.
With about 85% of a hike priced after a sharp rise, rate pricing is firmly in the zone to support a hike.
Hike pricing jumped from 35% two weeks ago, driven by Warsh's Jackson Hole speech and stronger labor and inflation data.
Warsh can point to Friday's twist flattening as proof that tighter policy builds credibility, which further justifies a hike.
If pricing stays stable and the Fed holds, it would be an unprecedented dovish hold: past holds came with far lower hike pricing than today's 22bps.
Warsh likely delivers a hawkish hike, with hawkish FOMC communications and a Jackson Hole-style presser; if wrong, a bigger Bessent 'house' is needed for the bond.
Sept FOMC communications likely lean hawkish, with the SEP showing 50bps of 2026 hikes, though Waller may dissent dovishly.
The presser should look more like Jackson Hole Warsh than July Warsh, given his Jackson Hole course correction and his aim of supporting the bond.
A hawkish hike should twist flatten the UST curve through higher front end and lower 30Y yields, challenging the belly view and supporting asset swap spreads.
If Warsh sounds impatient on inflation, markets raise and pull forward hikes, lifting 2Y rates 5-10bps, so higher front end rates follow.
A hawkish presser lowers 30Y rates by 5-10bps because of downside growth and inflation risk and a more credible, orthodox Fed.
A dovish presser cuts the expected hike peak and lifts 30Y rates about 5bps, due to dovish action and confusion over Warsh's reaction function.
A hawkish hike supports the constructive long end asset swap view, as lower growth and inflation risk and Fed credibility boost UST investor confidence.
With only one jobs report and one CPI before October, an October hike is expected unless data soften or Fed communication turns dovish.
The Trump admin faces a front end versus long end rate tradeoff; explained by Bessent and Warsh, Trump should grasp bond un-anchoring risks though he dislikes it.
Warsh faces a balancing act: signalling a hiking sequence could price over 100bp, while a dovish hike could raise doubts about the 2% commitment.
The USD outcome depends on the Fed out-hawking expectations and G10 peers, given a high bar, a sideways USD outlook and two-way risk.
Despite the prospect of hikes, the USD trades sideways into year-end: it is subdued, sentiment has soured and it has not rallied on energy, with a high out-hawk bar.
With over 3 Fed hikes priced and central banks repricing globally, the bar for the FOMC to out-hawk expectations and G10 peers is high.
The USD faces considerable two-way risk at the meeting, given bullish and bearish hike scenarios and sharp depreciation if the Fed holds.
A hike with a hawkish SEP, elevated forecasts and prolonged-campaign signals raises odds of 100bp or earlier hikes, supporting the USD; forward-guidance aversion challenges this.
Even with a hike, the USD could soften on dovish language, impatience with 'one and done', muddled messaging lifting back-end yields, or a restrained dot-plot.
